newsitem.title: SWEDEN: NORDIC SKIING-DAEHLIE SMASHES SVAN'S RECORD.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-DAEHLIE SMASHES SVAN'S RECORD.

text.p: Bjoern Daehlie of Norway won the season opening 10-km cross-country race on Saturday and in the process broke Swede Gunde Svan's record of Nordic skiing World Cup wins.
Before Saturday's freestyle race Daehlie and Svan had been level on 30 wins apiece.
"It is a bit special to beat Gunde Svan's record. He has always been my example and inspiration," said Daehlie after crossing the line 26 seconds clear of second-placed Jari Isometsa of Finland.
In the women's opening race, a five-km freestyle, Yelena Valbe snatched her 38th World Cup win, finishing a comfortable 10 seconds ahead of Italy's Stefania Belmondo.

While Daehlie coped easily with the soft Kiruna snow, Kazakhstan's strongly-built Vladimir Smirnov, who has 28 World Cup wins, appeared to find the going tough and could manage only ninth, more than a minute slower than the winner.
Daehlie said he did not wish to peak too early in the season as in some previous years. "I want to be at my best at the end of February when the world championships take place in Trondheim," he said.
Isometsa, third in last season's World Cup standings, gave notice in this opening race that he will again pose a threat to Daehlie and Smirnov.
